title: Bridging Teacher-Student Capability Gaps with Recurrent Computation
abstract: arXiv:2611.28603v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers capabilities from large language models to smaller students, yet stronger teachers do not always yield better students. Recent studies report diminishing or even negative returns from teacher scaling. We hypothesize that these limitations arise in part from insufficient student capacity to absorb the teacher's knowledge. We therefore investigate loop and recurrent computation as a way to expand the student's effective capacity by modifying its computation graph while keeping the backbone parameter count fixed. Under teacher-forced KD during pretraining, weight-shared looping improves performance but retains teacher-size saturation, whereas cross-token recurrence avoids the observed reversal with larger teachers. In mathematical post-training under both teacher-forced KD and on-policy distillation (OPD), recurrent students scale better with increasing teacher size than looped and vanilla LLMs do. Crucial

translated_title: 用循环计算弥合师生能力差距
translated_abstract: 知识蒸馏将大型语言模型的能力迁移到较小的学生模型，然而更强的教师模型并不总能产生更好的学生模型。近期研究报告称，教师模型规模的扩大甚至会带来收益递减或负收益。我们假设这些局限性部分源于学生模型缺乏足够的容量来吸收教师的知识。因此，我们研究循环计算，通过在保持骨干参数数量不变的情况下修改计算图，来扩展学生模型的有效容量。在预训练阶段的教师强制知识蒸馏（teacher-forced KD）下，权重共享的循环能提升性能，但仍存在教师规模饱和现象，而跨token循环则避免了随教师增大而出现的性能逆转。在数学后训练中，无论是教师强制知识蒸馏还是在线策略蒸馏（OPD），循环学生模型随教师规模增长的扩展性都优于循环结构和普通LLM。至关重要的是……
tldr: 该论文提出利用循环计算（尤其是跨token循环）在不增加参数量的前提下扩展学生模型的有效容量，从而弥合知识蒸馏中的师生能力差距，使学生模型能随更大规模的教师模型持续获益。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes using recurrent computation—especially cross-token recurrence—to expand the student's effective capacity without increasing parameters, bridging the teacher-student capability gap so that students scale better with larger teachers in knowledge distillation.
